title: Apple’s failed self-driving car program left a legacy of powerful AI chips
slides: Why did Apple kill its self-driving car?
The car project consumed billions of dollars over ten years.
It never drove a single mile autonomously on public roads.
That failure gave birth to chips now powering Apple's AI servers.
Your next iPhone runs on technology born from a dead car.
thread_text:
1. The project that never moved

Apple spent ten years and billions of dollars on a self-driving car that never drove autonomously on a public road.

2. Where the money really went

The car's failure pushed engineers to repurpose the silicon into chips now running Apple's AI servers.

3. The chip that escaped the wreck

Those server chips are a direct ancestor of the neural engine in your next iPhone.

4. A dead project resurrected

What was a total loss in one division became the backbone of Apple's entire AI infrastructure.

5. Check your phone tonight

Open Settings > General > About and look for 'Neural Engine'. Does that feature exist without a failed car?
